newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics lawsuit dismissed - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics lawsuit dismissed - NYT.

text.p: A lawsuit accusing Silicon Graphics Inc executives of defrauding investors has been dismissed by a federal judge, the New York Times said.
In Friday's edition, the Times said that the dismissal is likely to send the case to the appellate court, which could settle a new law aimed at blocking frivolous securities suits.

The suit had contended that Silicon Graphics officials had sold stock in the company while they knew that growth forecasts it was issuing were wrong, the Times said. The company has denied the charges.
Bruce Vanyo, a lawyer who represented the company, said the ruling meant that lawyers for shareholders would "have to conduct real investigations before bringing a lawsuit."
But William Lerach, a lawyer who represented the plaintiffs, said the ruling "will make it virtually impossible for victims of securities fraud to go to court to get their money back."

Federal Judge Fern Smith in her ruling cited a 1995 law designed to curb frivilous securities lawsuits. The judge said the plaintiffs had to "provide more details about the alleged negative internal reports."

"The allegations should include the titles of the reports, when they were prepared, who prepared them, to whom they were directed, their content, and the sources from which plaintiffs obtained this information," Smith said.
However, Lerach, the plaintiffs' lawyer, said it would be nearly impossible to meet those standards before the discovery phase of a lawsuit.
